about: The customer message writer's eval (contracts ask-skills/customer-message, tooling/scripts/evals/customer-message.mjs). Each case is a made-up business and the message Ask's card asked for, its versions the first draft as the palette writes one today. The writer writes it again; code checks it (checks.ts) and a judge reads it against the rubric (rubric.ts). `expect` adds patterns (read with the values taken out) a case's own words must or must not hold. Run it only on Ruben's word: it spends the eval key.

cases.note: A thin draft becomes a fuller message from the same facts: no price, no date, the opt-out line last.

business.name: Harbor Dental
business.tone: Warm and brief. Friendly, a sentence or two at a time, and straight to what the customer asked.

whatsapp.body: Hi {{1}}, we haven't seen you at {{2}} since the summer and we'd love to have you back. Book your next appointment here: {{3}} Reply STOP to opt out.

email.subject: We miss you
email.body: Hi {{1}}, it's been a while. Book again here: {{3}}

cases.note: Natural Spanish, tú throughout, ¡ and ¿ where they belong, the Spanish opt-out line.

cases.note: An offer with the owner's own figure and month: both kept exactly, nothing added.

Reply STOP to opt out

email.subject: 20% off class packs in November

cases.note: News with no price in the draft: no free estimate, no discount, no number invented.

business.name: Ridgeline Plumbing
business.tone: Straightforward and friendly. Plain words, no jargon.

whatsapp.body: Hi {{1}}, we now install water heaters too. If yours is getting old, book a time with us: {{2}} Reply STOP to opt out.

cases.note: Utility: about their booking only. The text fits one part with its values and the STOP line, and names the business first.

whatsapp.body: Hi {{1}}, this is a reminder of your appointment at {{2}} on {{3}}. If you need to change it, just reply to this message and we'll find another time for you.

sms.body: Hi {{1}}, this is a reminder of your appointment at {{2}} on {{3}}. If you need to change it, just reply to this message and we'll find another time.

cases.note: Spanish, de usted throughout, no exclamation marks; the text within two parts with its accents.

business.name: Estudio Legal Ramírez

whatsapp.body: Hola {{1}}! Te esperamos en {{2}} el {{3}}. Si necesitas cambiarla avísanos.

sms.body: Hola {{1}}, recuerda tu reunión en {{2}} el {{3}}. Si necesitas cambiarla, responde a este mensaje.

cases.note: The draft slips a promotion into a utility message: the writer drops it and says so in could_not.

whatsapp.body: Hi {{1}}, your session is confirmed for {{2}}. While you're here, ask about our new membership deals! See you soon.

cases.note: A review ask after a booking: utility, thanks first, the review link as the one call to act.

business.name: Paws & Co Grooming

We're open our usual hours, so come by whenever is easiest for you, and if you have any questions at all about it, or need us to hold it a little longer, just reply to this text and we'll be happy to help.

cases.note: An email alone: a specific subject under 60, short paragraphs, the business signs off, no unsubscribe of its own.

email.subject: NEW SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT FROM US
email.body: Hi {{1}}, we are happy to announce that {{2}} now offers irrigation installs and repairs for your garden. Book a time: {{3}}. To unsubscribe reply STOP.

cases.note: A closure notice with its own dates: kept exactly, no hours or reopening day invented.

whatsapp.body: Hi {{1}}, a heads-up: we're closed November 27 and 28 for Thanksgiving. Need to see us before then? Book here: {{2}} Reply STOP to opt out

cases.note: A Spanish offer with its own 2x1: kept exactly, the weekend kept, nothing added.

cases.note: A casual tone that welcomes emoji: still at most one, never in place of a word; the draft forgot the opt-out line, which an invitation to book again carries.

whatsapp.body: Hey {{1}} 🏄🌊🤙 thanks for your first lesson with us!!! 🎉🎉 Want to book the next one? {{2}} 😎

cases.note: The owner gave the day they open again and Ask's draft dropped it: the writer says it, from their own words, and adds nothing else.
